g1.label: A small ___ ran across the hot rock.
g1.why: A lizard is a small four-legged reptile — unlike a snake, it can run.

g2.label: Out in the outback, families use a ___ to get internet.
g2.why: A satellite sends signals back to earth, which is how remote homes get internet.

g3.label: Some beaches are ___ so that people can swim safely.
g3.why: To net off is to close an area with a net, so swimmers are protected from stingers.

g4.label: The local surf lifesaving ___ trains volunteers every summer.
g4.why: An association is an organised group with a shared aim, such as a lifesaving club.

g5.label: Walking off the path can ___ the plants.
g5.why: To damage something is to harm it so it no longer works or grows well.

g6.label: The box jellyfish is one of the most ___ animals in the sea.
g6.why: Deadly means able to kill you.

g7.label: The wet sand ___ in the early morning sun.
g7.why: To gleam is to shine softly — wet sand catches the light this way.

g8.label: There is always a ___ of sunburn in the Australian summer.
g8.why: A risk is the chance that something bad happens — the opposite of safety.

g9.label: A ___ of tiny islands lay just off the coast.
g9.why: A cluster is a small group close together, so it fits islands lying side by side.

g10.label: This rock is a sacred Aboriginal ___.
g10.why: A site is a place of importance, and Aboriginal sites are protected.

g11.label: She picked up a beautiful ___ from the wet sand.
g11.why: A seashell is the hard cover left by a small sea animal, found on the sand.

g12.label: Please take your ___ home with you and keep the beach clean.
g12.why: Litter is rubbish left lying in a public place.

g13.label: We ate breakfast outside on the ___.
g13.why: A terrace is the flat outdoor area by a house where you can sit and eat.

g14.label: Australians often say '___' instead of 'hello'.
g14.why: G'day is the everyday Australian greeting, used where British English says hello.

g15.label: I did not mean to listen, but I ___ their whole conversation.
g15.why: To overhear is to hear something by accident, not on purpose — you were not trying to listen.

g16.label: Our host ___ around the farm and explained everything.
g16.why: To show someone around is to take them through a place and explain it.

g17.label: Signs on the beach warn tourists about ___ in the water.
g17.why: Marine stinger is the general Australian term for any sea creature that stings.

g18.label: We followed a narrow ___ through the forest.
g18.why: A track is a rough, narrow path through the countryside.

g19.label: In summer, backpackers earn money by ___ fruit on farms.
g19.why: To pick fruit is to take it from the plant by hand.

g20.label: Few people live in the ___ of the country.
g20.why: The interior is the inland part of a country, far from the coast.

g21.label: Two swimmers ___ and had to be rescued by helicopter.
g21.why: To be swept out to sea is to be carried away from the shore. It is passive, because the water does it to you.

g22.label: On Sunday the neighbours invited us to a ___ in their garden.
g22.why: Barbie is the Australian short form of barbecue.

g23.label: Her ___ words helped him stop worrying.
g23.why: Comforting words make a worried person feel better.

g24.label: We saw a ___ rock rising out of the desert.
g24.why: Giant describes size, not danger: the rock is extremely large.

g25.label: The café ___ breakfast until eleven o'clock.
g25.why: To serve is to give food or drink to someone — what a café does.

g26.label: The lifeguards are there for your ___.
g26.why: Safety is being free from danger — the opposite of risk.

g27.label: Rain is not ___ in the desert at this time of year.
g27.why: Likely means probable. After is, use the adjective likely.

g28.label: Never walk in the outback ___ — always take a friend.
g28.why: On your own means with nobody else. In a real sentence the phrase takes your, not one's.

g29.label: They ___ into the bush without telling anyone where they were going.
g29.why: To go off means to leave a place, often suddenly.

g30.label: In the desert, water is the key to ___.
g30.why: Survival is staying alive in danger, which in a desert depends on water.

g31.label: In summer the ___ makes swimming dangerous in northern Australia.
g31.why: The box jellyfish is one specific jellyfish whose sting can kill, not stinging sea life in general.

g32.label: The ___ of the hostel showed us to our room.
g32.why: The owner is the person a business or object belongs to.

g33.label: A strong ___ can pull a swimmer far away from the beach.
g33.why: A rip current pulls swimmers away from the beach, which is what makes it dangerous.

g34.label: Do not ___ the birds while they are nesting.
g34.why: To disturb is to interrupt — nesting birds must be left alone.

g35.label: ___ is popular with tourists who want to see the real Australia.
g35.why: Bushwalking is the Australian word for hiking through the countryside.

g36.label: The centre of Australia is ___ dry, empty land.
g36.why: Mostly means in most cases — it says how much of the land is dry.

g37.label: The search was ___ when it got dark.
g37.why: To call off means to cancel something that was planned, such as a search.

g38.label: When the farmer broke his leg, the ___ flew him to hospital.
g38.why: An air ambulance flies injured people to hospital — vital where farms are hours from a road.

g39.label: The ___ conditions in the outback are hard for farmers.
g39.why: Climatic describes conditions to do with the weather of a region.

g40.label: Be careful where you walk — a ___ can hide in the long grass.
g40.why: A snake is a legless reptile, and long grass is exactly where one can hide.

g41.label: The club's ___ spoke to the newspaper about beach safety.
g41.why: A spokesperson speaks officially on behalf of a group.

g42.label: We slept in a cheap ___ near the beach in Cairns.
g42.why: A youth hostel is cheap shared accommodation, which is why backpackers stay in one.
